notes.body: The boy lays his whole fortune out in five shares, and the point is never the money — each share is a different piece of inner work: alms to purify what's visible, a portion kept as a standing reminder of past sin, gratitude held in trust until he's wise enough to spend it, generosity handed over face to face, and love for his teacher. The amounts don't matter; the mechanisms do. And notice the scholar won't let him dispense the purification share at all — that one isn't his to give away. It's a trust held for the rightful master until he meets him.
notes.quote: This is all my wealth, in front of you, in five shares

notes.body: When the scholar leaves and comes back, the boy has gone weak and yellow, and the text names the cause plainly: this is the wasting of a lover parted from the beloved, not a fever. Think of the reed cut from the reed-bed and hollowed into a flute — the ache in its sound is pure longing for the ground it was torn from. The boy's failing body is that same cry written into flesh, and the longing itself is the proof that the union was real.
notes.quote: That is from a loneliness that hit me after you went

notes.body: At the door the Shaykh asks the boy's name, and when he answers 'this scholar set me free,' the Shaykh asks: if your teacher is himself owned and owns nothing, can he really free you? A prisoner cannot unlock another prisoner's chains. One by one every badge the boy carried to that door — his teacher, his learning, his hard-won freedom — is stripped away, until he's empty enough for the real teaching to finally begin.
notes.anchor: a prisoner cannot free a prisoner
notes.quote: if this scholar were himself owned and did not own — would his freeing you be valid

notes.body: The seven-day wait and the seven circuits of the House aren't a test of patience — they're the boy learning his exact place. Picture a planet held around its sun: gravity acting as love, the planet forever falling toward the center while moving just fast enough never to crash in. Drift outward and you're lost in the cold void — death by isolation; fall straight in and you're consumed — death by overstepping your rank. The orbit is the narrow lane where love keeps you alive. His name binds him to a center he will circle but never own.
notes.quote: The name belongs to you, and you belong to the name
